info.title: Inference Gateway
info.description:
One endpoint and one key for every model your organisation uses.

**Inference** endpoints speak the OpenAI API (Chat Completions, Responses, embeddings, decisions) and the Anthropic Messages API, streaming or not, for any model behind the gateway. Authenticate with a virtual key (`sk-gw-…`) whose scope is `inference` or `all`, as `Authorization: Bearer` or `x-api-key`. The `model` is the model name chosen in the gateway.

The **admin API** (`/admin/api/…`) is what the console uses. Authenticate with the master key or a virtual key whose scope is `admin`, `all` or `project` (its project's keys, playground, request log and metrics only), as `Authorization: Bearer`, or with a console session cookie; requests with the cookie that change something also need an `x-gateway-csrf` header.

get.description:
RFC 8414. Clients identify with a Client ID Metadata Document (`client_id_metadata_document_supported`);
there is no dynamic client registration. PKCE S256, public clients only.

RFC 9728: where MCP clients sign in to use the gateway's MCP endpoints (`authorization_servers`).
Also at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/{server}`,
for one endpoint. A refused MCP request names it in its `WWW-Authenticate` header.

The deployment's provider model and the credential it calls with, as configured now;
none once the deployment is deleted.

tool_calls.description: The tools its response called, where its bodies are logged (see `capture`).

tool.description: The tool an MCP call (api `mcp`) called, on the server named by `model_name`.

task_state.description: A message to an A2A agent (api `a2a`): the state its task was left in, such as `completed`.

context_id.description: A message to an A2A agent: its context, shared by a conversation's messages.

parent_id.description: Set on the calls a routed request made (decision, routed call): the router's entry.

labels.description: The labels the client sent, as `{"key": "value"}`.

oneOf.description: What the guardrails did, stored with the entry.

searches.description: Searches billed: web searches a chat model ran, or a rerank model's searches.

bodies.description:
Whether its bodies were logged: `stored`, `truncated` (cut to the size limit), `expired`
(past their retention), `dropped` (could not be kept) or `deleted`; none when not logged.

McpAuth.description: How the gateway authenticates to an upstream: an MCP server or an A2A agent.

secret.description: Whether a secret was set on the exporting gateway. Never its value.

projects.description: The names of the projects it is limited to.

name.description: What clients call it by, at `/mcp/{name}`: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

url.description: The server's Streamable HTTP endpoint, such as `https://mcp.example.com/mcp`.

auth_header.description: The header that carries the secret, for `header` auth.

secret.description:
The token or API key the gateway sends, for `bearer` and `header` auth, or the OAuth client's
secret. Write-only; omitted on an update, the server keeps its secret.

oneOf.description: The OAuth client, for `oauth` and `oauth_user` auth.

tags.description: A key with tags may only use untagged servers and those sharing a tag with it.

project_ids.description: Projects the server is limited to; empty means any key may use it (as its tags allow).

timeout_secs.description: Seconds a POST may take, its streamed answer included. Default 300.

allowed_tools.description: The tools keys may call; empty (the default) for every tool the server offers, new ones included.

denied_tools.description: Tools keys may not call, whatever `allowed_tools` says.

price_per_call.description: USD per tool call, charged once the tool answered. Default 0.

tool_prices.description: USD per call of these tools, instead of `price_per_call`.

server_info.description: The server's `serverInfo`: its name and version.

error.description: Why the server could not be used, when `ok` is false.

has_secret.description: Whether a secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

oauth.description: The OAuth client, for `oauth` and `oauth_user` auth.

allowed_tools.description: The tools keys may call; empty for every tool the server offers.

denied_tools.description: Tools keys may not call, whatever `allowed_tools` says.

price_per_call.description: USD per tool call, unless `tool_prices` names the tool.

tool_prices.description: USD per call of these tools.

MessagesRequest.description: An Anthropic Messages request. Any other field of the Anthropic API is accepted.

max_tokens.description: Defaults to the deployment's `default_max_tokens` when omitted.

model.description: The public model name: a deployment's or an auto router's.

metadata.description:
Replaces the stored metadata; `{}` removes it. `display_name`, `vendor` and `description`, when
present, are strings.

Mode.description: What a deployment serves, and so which endpoints route to it.

shutdown_date.description:
When the model will shut down (`YYYY-MM-DD`), from the price catalog; null if not
announced.

ModelExtendedEntry.description:
A model with what the gateway knows about it. Where a model has several deployments, or
is an auto router, the limits are the lowest among them and `structured_outputs` is true
only if all of them support it.

shutdown_date.description:
When the model will shut down (`YYYY-MM-DD`), from the price catalog; null if not
announced.

mode.description: What the model serves. Auto routers are `chat`.

max_input_tokens.description: From the price catalog; null if unknown.

max_output_tokens.description: From the price catalog; null if unknown.

structured_outputs.description: Whether the model supports JSON schema output, from the price catalog. False if unknown.

tags.description: The model's deployment tags, or an auto router's own tags.

model.description: The public model name: a deployment's, an auto router's or an alias's, in the file or on the gateway.

metadata.description: `display_name`, `vendor` and `description`, and any other fields; `{}` removes the model's metadata.

ModelsAnswer.description:
The models a key may use, in the OpenAI format, or in Anthropic's for clients that send
`anthropic-version`.

NamedItem.description: A key or project as a picker offers it.

OAuthConfig.description: An upstream's OAuth client, as configured.

resource.description: The RFC 8707 resource the tokens are for, such as the MCP server's URL.

redirect_uri.description:
The redirect URI the client was registered with, for `oauth_user`. Without one, the
gateway's address as the console reaches it, followed by `/admin/auth/oauth/callback`.

token_auth.description:
How the client authenticates at the token URL: `client_secret_basic` (the default with a
secret), `client_secret_post`, or `none` (a public client).

sign_in_by.description:
For `oauth_user`: the request labels that tell a key's sign-ins apart, `tenant` or `tenant`
and `user`. Empty: the key signs in once.

sign_in_retention_days.description:
For `oauth_user`: how many days a sign-in is kept unused before it is deleted, 1 to 90;
`SIGN_IN_RETENTION_DAYS` when not set.

client_secret.description: Omitted or null keeps the stored secret; an empty string removes it (public client).

user_role.description: Signs in as a user, who sees only the projects an admin adds them to. None: admins only.

OidcTest.description: Whether the identity provider's discovery worked: its authorization endpoint, or the error.

OpenAiError.description: An error, in the OpenAI API's format.

param.description: Always null: the gateway does not say which parameter was wrong.

code.description: Such as `content_filter`, when a guardrail refused the prompt.

PersonRole.description: An admin may do everything; a user only works in the projects an admin adds them to.

PersonView.description: Someone who signed in, with the projects they work in (users only; admins see every project).

enforced.description: Set on the key or its project: every request goes through it.

web_search.description: Requests may have it search the web: it has a web search, and the key and its project allow it.

PlaygroundOptions.description:
What the playground offers for a key: the models it may call, the guardrails a request may
ask for (those the key or its project enforce marked), and the MCP servers and A2A agents it
may use.

PlaygroundUpstream.description: An MCP server or A2A agent the key may use, or a tool router.

needs_sign_in.description: The key signs in to it itself, and has not yet.

router.description: A tool router, listed with the MCP servers: requests name it like one.

guardrails.description: The names of the guardrails every request of its keys goes through.

enabled.description: While false, the project's keys are refused like disabled keys.

max_budget_usd.description: Budget in USD per `budget_period`, on top of each key's own; both None = unlimited.

guardrail_ids.description: Guardrails every request of the project's keys goes through. Omitted, they stay as they are.

web_search.description: While false, no key in the project may have the model search the web, whatever its own setting.

prompt_logging.description:
Whether its keys' prompts and responses are logged, for debugging: `deny` (the default),
`allow` for the keys that opt in, or `force` for every key.

ProjectRow.description:
A group of virtual keys. It organises the console and can block its keys: while inactive,
they are refused like disabled keys. It grants, limits and budgets nothing.

max_budget_usd.description: Budget per `budget_period`, on top of each key's own; None = unlimited.

spend_reset_at.description: Set by "reset spend": the current period counts only spend after this.

guardrail_ids.description: Guardrails every request of the project's keys goes through.

web_search.description:
Whether its keys' requests may have the model search the web. False forbids it for every
key in the project, whatever the key's own says.

prompt_logging.description:
Whether its keys' prompts and responses are logged, for debugging: never, where a key
opts in, or always (see `api::prompt_logged`).

keys.description: How many keys the project groups.

oneOf.description: Current budget period and its spend; None for unlimited projects.

PromptLogging.description: A project's (or, for keys outside projects, the gateway's) prompt logging policy.

ProviderAnswer.description:
The provider's answer, in the API's own format: a JSON object, or server-sent events when
streaming. Responses carry `x-request-id`, and routed ones `x-gateway-routed-model` and
`x-gateway-route`.

Ready.description: What readiness depends on, and whether each is there.

ReasoningEffort.description:
A reasoning effort, in order: every level OpenAI's and Anthropic's APIs take. Which a model
accepts comes from its price catalog entry (see `Deployment::efforts`); translated requests get
the nearest of those.

RerankRequest.description: A rerank request, as Cohere's API takes it.

documents.description: Up to 1,000 documents: strings, or objects with a `text`.

top_n.description: How many of the most relevant documents to return (default: all).

return_documents.description: Include each document's text in the results.

max_tokens_per_doc.description: Cohere models only: truncate documents to this many tokens.

RerankResponse.description: Ranked documents, most relevant first, as Cohere's v2 API returns them.

id.description: The request's id, as in the request log.

index.description: The document's position in the request.

ResponsesRequest.description: An OpenAI Responses request. Any other field of the OpenAI API is accepted.

input.description: A string or a list of input items.

previous_response_id.description:
Continue a conversation. Works on every model: the gateway keeps the history for
providers that do not, until it goes unused for the `response_ttl_minutes` setting, within
the key's quota.

store.description: Defaults to true; false keeps no history.

background.description: Refused: the gateway can neither account for nor retrieve background responses.

Route.description:
One option of an auto router: a named pool of chat models and when to use it. The decision
model picks a route by its name; the request then goes to one of its models at random.

name.description: What the decision model chooses, e.g. "Simple" or "Complex"; unique within the router.

RouteModel.description: A chat model in a route.

oneOf.description: Set on the requests the route sends to this model, replacing the client's; unset keeps it.

routes.description:
The routes to choose from: each a name, a description of when to use it, and the chat
models it sends requests to (one at random), with an optional reasoning effort each. A
route given as `{"model", "description"}`, as before, is a one-model route named after it.

fallback_route.description:
The name of the route used when the decision fails. Defaults to the first route.
`fallback_model` is accepted too, as before.

tags.description: Permission tags, with the same rule as a deployment's.

sticky.description:
Keep each conversation on the route and model its first turn was sent to, instead of
deciding every turn anew: the prompt cache stays warm and later turns need no decision.

missing.description:
Its decision model when no decision deployment has that name, and its routes' models that
no chat deployment has.

RouterListItem.description: A router in the list, with the models it names that no deployment serves.

sticky.description: Conversations stay on the route and model their first turn was sent to.

Secrets.description: Secret values of a credential. Entered through the admin API/UI and encrypted at rest.

google_service_account.description: Vertex: the service account key file (JSON), as downloaded from Google Cloud.

client_secret.description: Azure with Entra ID: the app registration's client secret, used instead of an API key.

ServiceAccountView.description: Who a Vertex credential's key file authenticates as.

SessionInfo.description: Who is signed in, and what the sign-in screen offers.

oneOf.description:
An admin may do everything; a user only works in `projects`. Null while signed out. The
console shows a user only their projects' keys, playground, request log and metrics.

projects.description: A user's projects; null for an admin.

oneOf.description: Set when single sign-on is enabled.

master_key.description: Whether `GATEWAY_MASTER_KEY` is set; without it, single sign-on is the only sign-in.

dev.description: Local development builds: the sign-in screen offers Dev Login.

version.description: The git tag the gateway was built from, shown on the sign-in screen and in the console header.

api_docs.description: Whether `/admin/openapi.json` and the API reference at `/admin/docs/` are served.

SessionUser.description:
Who signed in: a person (`id`, `email`, `name`), a virtual key (`id`, `name`), or Dev Login
(`name`, and the local development user's `id`).

email.description:
Only for a person, and null when the identity provider gave none: the outer `Option` says
whether the field is sent at all.

max_attempts.description: Deployments tried per request on rate limits, server errors and timeouts.

cooldown_secs.description: How long a failing deployment is skipped.

adaptive_routing.description:
Deployments get less traffic while their recent calls fail or are slow (see `router`).
Off, requests spread by the configured weights only.

sticky_routing.description:
Conversations stay on the deployment, and on an auto router the route, that served them
(see `affinity`). Off, every request is balanced on its own.

reload_secs.description:
Periodic full reload of the configuration from Postgres, in addition to the instant
updates over Valkey: it covers updates a replica missed.

request_log_retention_days.description: Days request logs, and so metrics, are kept: 7 to 1080, or 0 to keep them forever.

audit_log_retention_days.description:
Days audit log entries are kept: 7 to 1080, or 0 to keep them forever. Independent of the
request log's.

prompt_log_retention_days.description: Days logged prompts and responses are kept: 1 to 60, and no longer than the request log's.

prompt_log_max_kb.description: Largest logged request or response, in KB; longer strings in it are cut.

response_ttl_minutes.description:
How long a `previous_response_id` conversation can go unused and still be continued; each
continuation starts the time again.

conversation_quota_mb.description:
Conversation history one virtual key may keep in Valkey: the size of its conversations that
have not expired. Valkey also holds rate limits, budgets and sessions.

header_timeout_secs.description: Time a client has to send its request headers.

body_timeout_secs.description: Time a client has to send its whole request body. Responses are not limited.

max_connections.description: Open client connections; more wait in the listen backlog.

api_docs.description:
The OpenAPI document at `/admin/openapi.json` and the API reference at `/admin/docs/`, for
signed-in people and admin and project keys.

price_import.description: LiteLLM's price catalog is imported on a schedule (see `prices`). Off, only on demand.

price_import_hours.description: Hours between scheduled imports of the price catalog.

price_auto_accept.description:
After every import, deployments whose prices no longer match their catalog entry take the
catalog's prices, as the console's Accept button does (see `prices::accept_changes`).

prompt_logging.description:
Prompt logging for keys outside projects: `deny`, or `allow` for those that opt in. Never
`force`, which would log every admin key. Projects set their own.

defaults.description: What each setting is when it was never changed.

updated_at.description: When the settings were last saved; absent while they are all defaults.

SignIn.description: A key's sign-in to an upstream by labels.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used, at most an hour off.

SignInStatus.description: An upstream that keeps a sign-in per tenant or user, for the request's labels.

sign_in_by.description: The labels its sign-ins are told apart by.

signed_in.description: Whether the request's tenant or user has signed in.

missing_label.description: The label the request lacks for this upstream, if any.

Source.description: Whose text is checked: the prompt, or the model's response.

SsoButton.description: The single sign-on button on the sign-in screen.

Status.description: This replica, and how its configuration last loaded.

version.description: The git tag the gateway was built from.

registry_errors.description: Deployments, routers and aliases that could not be loaded, and why.

StoredBodies.description: How many prompts and responses are stored for a key or project.

assets.description: Images and other assets; TypeSafe deployments only, with `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true`.

TagUsage.description: A tag, with how many of each carry it.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers and A2A agents carrying the tag.

keys.description: Keys holding the tag (for a user, their projects' keys).

TestUsage.description: The tokens a passed test used; null where a decision model did not say.

TokenCount.description: A token count, as Anthropic's API answers it.

ToolRoute.description: A group of one MCP server's tools, offered when the decision model finds them needed.

name.description: Unique in its router: letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

description.description: When the tools are needed, for the decision model ("questions about invoices and payments").

server_id.description: The MCP server whose tools the route offers.

tools.description: The server's tools it offers, after the server's own filters; empty for all of them.

ToolRouteDoc.description: A route, with its MCP server by name.

name.description:
What requests name it by, like an MCP server: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and
no MCP server's name.

instructions.description: The question the decision model gets for every route; empty for the default.

threshold.description:
A route is offered when the decision model is at least this sure it is needed: above 0,
below 1. Default 0.5.

max_routes.description: At most this many routes per request, the surest first. Default: no limit.

ToolUse.description: A tool the latest logged responses called, with how many of them did (`recent_tools`).

outputs.description:
The texts as they may pass, one for each text checked: masked where something was masked.
When blocked, the guardrail's message instead, once.

Via.description: How a request signed in to the admin API.

scope.description: Whether the key calls the inference API, the admin API or both.

project_id.description: The project the key is grouped under in the console.

project_active.description: False while the key's project is inactive; the key is then refused like a disabled one.

allowed_tags.description: Deployment tags this key holds; empty means no tag restriction.

max_budget_usd.description: Budget per `budget_period` (day, week or month); None = unlimited.

spend_usd.description: Lifetime spend (informational; budgets use per-period spend).

spend_reset_at.description: Set by "reset spend": the current period counts only spend after this.

guardrail_ids.description: Guardrails every request of this key goes through, on top of its project's.

web_search.description:
Whether its requests may have the model search the web (billed per search). Its project
may forbid it anyway: see `api::web_search_allowed`.

prompt_logging.description:
Whether its prompts and responses are logged, where its project allows it. A project that
denies or forces logging decides instead: see `api::prompt_logged`.

admin_key.description: A virtual key whose scope is `admin`, `all` or `project` (its project only).

admin_session.name: gw_admin
admin_session.description: A console session. Requests that change something also need an `x-gateway-csrf` header (any value).

virtual_key.description: A virtual key, as OpenAI clients send it.

virtual_key_header.name: x-api-key
virtual_key_header.description: A virtual key, as Anthropic clients send it.
